title: Frequency adverbs + Present Simple review
grammarNote: НАРЕЧИЯ ЧАСТОТНОСТИ (Frequency adverbs) отвечают на вопрос "КАК ЧАСТО?" (How often?). Они используются с PRESENT SIMPLE, который описывает регулярные действия, привычки и общие факты. Правильное РАСПОЛОЖЕНИЕ наречия в предложении — одна из самых частых ошибок студентов.

grammarTable.subject: always
grammarTable.example: I always check Telegram before class. · She is always online.

grammarTable.subject: usually
grammarTable.example: He usually studies in the library. · They are usually punctual.

grammarTable.subject: often
grammarTable.example: We often watch tutorials on YouTube. · He is often tired.

grammarTable.subject: sometimes
grammarTable.example: I sometimes forget to charge my laptop. · She is sometimes late.

grammarTable.subject: rarely
grammarTable.example: He rarely uses Facebook. · She is rarely offline.

grammarTable.subject: never
grammarTable.example: I never use TikTok at work. · They are never on time.

grammarTable.subject: POSITION 1
grammarTable.example: I always check / She never posts / They often share

grammarTable.subject: POSITION 2
grammarTable.example: He is always late / She is never offline / I am usually tired

rows.example: I check my email every day. · She calls her parents every Sunday.

rows.form: once / twice / three times a day
rows.example: I use Anki twice a day. · He checks his phone about forty times a day!
I clean my room once a week. · We have IT classes twice a week.
She does yoga every other day. · I visit the library every other week.

rows.form: on Mondays / at weekends / in the morning
rows.example: On Mondays we have lectures. · At weekends I always sleep until 10.
How often do you check your phone? — About sixty times a day, sadly!

grammarExtra.title: Position rules — the most important grammar rule

rows.example: I always / usually / often CHECK my phone. ✅
She IS always / usually / often online. ✅

rows.form: ❌ NEVER put adverb after main verb
rows.example: ❌ I check always my phone. → ✅ I always check my phone.
❌ She always is online. → ✅ She is always online.

rows.form: sometimes / usually can go at start
rows.example: Sometimes I forget to charge my phone. (informal, emphatic)

rows.form: never/always can NOT go at start
rows.example: ❌ Always I check Telegram. → ✅ I always check Telegram.

grammarExtra.title: Present Simple: positive, negative, question review

rows.form: I / You / We / They + base verb
rows.example: I use Instagram. · They check emails every morning.
She uses Telegram. · He watches tutorials every evening.
I don't use TikTok. · She doesn't post selfies.
Do you use LinkedIn? · Does he check email daily?
Do you use Anki? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
How often do you check your phone? · What does she use?
✅ I always check my email. (adverb BEFORE main verb!)
✅ She is always busy. (adverb AFTER "be"!)

rows.form: ❌ He use social media every day.
rows.example: ✅ He uses social media every day. (3rd person → -s!)
✅ Does she use Instagram? (after does → base form!)

grammarTip:
ПОЗИЦИЯ наречия частотности — два правила, которые НУЖНО знать:

① С обычным глаголом → ПЕРЕД глаголом:
   I ALWAYS check / She NEVER posts / They OFTEN share

② С глаголом BE → ПОСЛЕ него:
   He IS always late / She IS never offline / I AM usually tired

💡 Мнемоника: 'be' = 'быть' — наречие ПОСЛЕ него, потому что 'be' отвечает само за себя!

⚠️ Всегда помни: He/She/It в Present Simple → verb + -s:
   She always CHECKS (не 'check'!) · He usually WATCHES (не 'watch'!)

exercises.text: I ___ check ___ my messages before breakfast.
exercises.hint: adverb + main verb: I always check. (not "I check always").
With "be": She is always online. (adverb AFTER "be").

exercises.text: Amir ___ (check) his phone about 60 times a day.
She ___ use TikTok — she thinks it wastes time.
I use Anki ___ — morning and evening.
exercises.hint: Twice = two times. Morning + evening = two times → twice a day.

exercises.text: "She always is late" is correct English.
exercises.hint: With "be": adverb goes AFTER "be". ✅ She is always late.

opts: He is check Facebook every day.
exercises.hint: He = 3rd person → checks. Present Simple, no -ing.

exercises.instruction: Write the adverb that means "0% of the time".
exercises.text: I ___ watch TV — I only use YouTube.
exercises.hint: never = 0% of the time. Position: before main verb.

exercises.text: "___ does she check her email?" — "Every morning at 8."
exercises.hint: "How often?" asks about frequency. "Every morning" = the answer.

exercises.instruction: Which adverb fits? (about 80% of the time)
exercises.text: He ___ uses Google Docs for lecture notes.
exercises.hint: usually ≈ 80% of the time. Not always, but most of the time.

exercises.text: "Sometimes I forget to charge my laptop" is correct.
exercises.hint: "sometimes" can go at the beginning of a sentence for emphasis. ✅

questions.text: "I ___ check my phone first thing in the morning." (100%)
Correct position: "She ___ is ___ late for class."
questions.hint: With "be": She IS always late. Adverb after "be".

questions.text: Zhibek ___ (use) Instagram for dance content every evening.
"He ___ Facebook — he says it's for old people." (0%)
questions.hint: never = 0%, placed before the main verb.

questions.text: "I check always my Telegram messages" is correct.
questions.hint: Adverb goes BEFORE main verb: "I always check my Telegram messages." ✅

questions.text: I use Anki in the morning AND in the evening. That's ___.
questions.hint: Twice = two times. Morning + evening = twice a day.

questions.text: ___ she use LinkedIn? — Yes, she does.
questions.hint: She = 3rd person → Does + subject + base verb?

questions.text: "Does she uses Twitter?" — what is wrong?
questions.hint: After Does → base form: Does she USE? (never "uses" after does/do).

questions.text: He ___ go to the IT office — he fixes everything himself.
questions.hint: rarely = almost never (about 20% of the time).
"How often?" = asking about frequency: always, sometimes, twice a week, etc.

questions.text: "Sometimes I forget to charge my laptop" — is this correct?
questions.hint: "sometimes" can go at the start of a sentence for emphasis. ✅

questions.text: Kamila ___ (not / use) Facebook — she says it's for parents.
questions.hint: She → doesn't + base verb: doesn't use.

questions.text: "She is never ___." — what kind of word fills the blank?
questions.hint: She is never [offline/late/available] — adjective/adverb after "be never".
"be" → adverb after it: She IS always late. ✅

questions.text: How ___ do you check social media? — About twenty times a day!
